challenge: Determine a native binding strength from the first byte of the SHA-256 of the unmodified official 80-cell carrier (4 plus the byte modulo 8). This selection has no measured-particle input. Use the next byte modulo 17 minus 8 as a common per-load energy shift. Compare the native law and its pair-mobility-assisted competitor.
preparation: In one path a compact pair at translation character zero evolves. In the other, two independent uniform singles evolve on two identical rings. Recombine both arms. For motion, evolve a compact cluster in one of two copies at character zero or the chosen nonzero character. All inactive copies are parked; the active load is equal in both arms. Read both quadratures.
gate: Write the prediction from only the clock and binding counts before generating motion. Run both laws with the same source realization and exposures. For every 2..5 body sector and both momenta retain interval overlap or exclusion or unresolved. Require a dominant weight >= 0.95 for a source assignment and a relative interval span <= 16 percent for a resolved comparison. Retain both failures and successes.
exposure: Use the common material-inertia clock and shot protocol. Higher-body measurements on this ring are an additional test. The 12-,16-,24-port results and the known XXZ identity motivated it.
